newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle priced at $67 - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle priced at $67 - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle owners were pricing cattle at $67 per cwt early Monday with packer bids awaited, feedlot sources said.
They noted that packers bought a lot of cattle last week and may not bid aggressively on Monday. Last week's purchases were, however, being picked up fairly quickly.

"They shipped a lot of cattle Friday and Saturday," one Kansas dealer said, noting that more than two-thirds of his sales had already been shipped. USDA reported 133,500 head traded in Texas/west Oklahoma last week and 103,700 head in Kansas, leaving feedlots fairly current on marketings.
One Texas dealer reported that some of the cattle he sold were being shipped to Kansas and Colorado.
"They are short of cattle up north," he said.
Strength in boxed beef prices were seen helping to support prices. USDA boxed beef cut-out values Friday were up $1.50 to $0.78 per cwt.
